D.t: Jermaine Johnson trails by 6.7 and wins 16% of simulations. Closing it takes about 67,806 voters switching sides, or 135,612 more net votes from new turnout.
In 8 of 10 simulations the result lands between R +15.1 and D +2.2. A normal polling error decides it.
The polls page average is R +9.7. Your best recent poll is New York Times/Siena at R +7.7; your worst is Trafalgar Group (R) at R +14.9. 7 polls in the last 30 days.

The biggest vote banks for Democrats: Richland, a projected net 76,363 votes; Charleston, a projected net 34,059 votes; Orangeburg, a projected net 12,789 votes. Every point of extra turnout here is worth more than persuasion anywhere else.
The large counties within 12 points: York, R +7.7, 5.7% of the vote; Berkeley, R +3.6, 4.3% of the vote; Beaufort, R +5.1, 4.1% of the vote; Dorchester, R +1.4, 3.0% of the vote.

D.h: Where you run behind the 2024 map
D.t: Against the 2024 presidential vote, Jermaine Johnson runs furthest behind in Pickens, Oconee, Anderson. That is where the forecast sees voters who backed your side two years ago and have not come back yet.

Groups big enough to move the race: White voters, 75% of voters, 36 to 61, where a 5 point gain is worth 3.75 points; Voters who cast ballots in 2022 and 2024, 66% of voters, 45 to 52, where a 5 point gain is worth 3.29 points; Voters without a degree, 62% of voters, 46 to 50, where a 5 point gain is worth 3.12 points.
The forecast's worst groups for Jermaine Johnson: Immigration voters 12 to 85, White voters 36 to 61, Incomes $125K and up 37 to 60. Cutting the loss here is often cheaper than winning new groups.
$136K cash against $1.7M. Outspent: lean on earned media, digital, field and the outside groups, and pick the two or three media markets that decide it.
Cash: $1.7M in the bank against $136K for Jermaine Johnson.
